# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The baseline passes simulation and uses 15 LUTs, 6 FFs, no DSP48s or BRAM, but routed setup WNS is −0.946 ns while hold WHS is +0.167 ns, so timing is not closed. The reported critical path runs from `rd_ptr` through distributed-memory read logic to `out_last`; the advisor attributes much of the delay to the output pad and clock insertion. The top’s authoritative latency is 1 cycle, and the objective is to establish timing feasibility before seeking LUT savings.

## Hypothesis
Caching the FIFO head tuple in output registers and driving the output ports directly from those registers should remove the pointer-to-memory-read path at the pads and may recover setup timing, at the cost of roughly WIDTH+1 additional FFs.

## Instruction for generator
In `packet_fifo_core`, add head data and last registers and drive `out_data` and `out_last` directly from them; update the cached tuple on an empty push, and on a pop load the next queued tuple, handling simultaneous pop/push at occupancy one by caching the incoming tuple. Preserve the ring buffer, exact occupancy and ready/valid behavior, reset priority, parameterized widths and depths, full simultaneous transfers, and minimum accepted-transfer age; leave invalid payload unspecified and keep the top’s `// @latency 1` annotation. The cached outputs must stay stable during stalls, and the changed child must remain live-reached from `packet_fifo` and pass the unchanged parameter-matrix testbench and all routed metric gates.
